$comment: Held-out evaluation labels (scripts/eval.py). knownPositives come from a code audit by an AI agent (Claude) that read only the project's source at the pinned revision: it did not run Midwrite and did not see its output. findings are classified afterwards, finding by finding, with the Phase 2 classes. No independent human review has been performed; an AI agent checking another AI agent's results is not independent human validation. Corrections go in `corrections` with a reason, never by editing a label to raise a score.

knownPositives.scope: unhandled half-written-state windows in server code; the audit was capped at 30 entries, highest confidence first, so the list is a sample when the project has more

findings.by: AI agent (Claude), finding-by-finding source review, separate from the auditor; did not see knownPositives

knownPositives.dbAccess: drizzle neon-http, no transaction; one autocommitted db.insert(plans).onConflictDoUpdate per variant inside the for...of loop (via nested helper _addVariant)
knownPositives.firstEffect: _addVariant(...) at line 233 -> db.insert(plans).values(variant).onConflictDoUpdate at line 166 for an earlier variant
knownPositives.secondEffect: _addVariant(...) at line 233 -> db.insert(plans)...onConflictDoUpdate at line 166 for a later variant (getProduct at line 200 and listPrices at line 203 run in between and throw via the SDK onError hook in configureLemonSqueezy)
knownPositives.consequence: A crash, timeout or Lemon Squeezy API error mid-loop leaves the plan table holding only some of the store's subscription variants. The only caller (src/components/dashboard/billing/plans/plans.tsx:34) runs syncPlans only when the plan table is empty, so the partial write disarms the sync trigger: the missing plans are never synced, are never shown or purchasable, and subscription webhooks for those variants are recorded as 'Plan with variantId ... not found' (src/lib/webhook.ts:88-89) so the subscription row is never created. Nothing repairs it.

knownPositives.dbAccess: drizzle neon-http, no transaction; storeWebhookEvent autocommits the webhookEvent insert, processWebhookEvent later autocommits the subscription upsert and the processed=true update as separate statements
knownPositives.firstEffect: storeWebhookEvent(...) at line 47 -> db.insert(webhookEvents) processed=false at src/lib/webhook.ts:31
knownPositives.secondEffect: processWebhookEvent(...) at line 49 -> db.insert(subscriptions).onConflictDoUpdate at src/lib/webhook.ts:126 and db.update(webhookEvents).set({processed: true}) at src/lib/webhook.ts:144
knownPositives.consequence: A crash/timeout, or a getPrice failure (the SDK onError hook throws) after the event row is stored leaves a webhookEvent row with processed=false and the subscription not upserted. No code ever re-reads or replays unprocessed events. Lemon Squeezy redelivers the failed webhook, but storeWebhookEvent gives each delivery a fresh random id, so the original row stays processed=false forever (a stored but never-processed event). The subscription change is applied only if a redelivery succeeds; once the retries are used up it is lost even though the payload is stored.

knownPositives.dbAccess: drizzle neon-http, no transaction; subscription upsert and webhookEvent processed-flag update are separate autocommitted statements
knownPositives.secondEffect: db.update(webhookEvents).set({ processed: true, processingError }) at line 144
knownPositives.consequence: A crash between the two leaves the subscription row already updated while its webhookEvent record still says processed=false. Lemon Squeezy's redelivery re-applies the idempotent upsert under a new event row (fresh random id), so the original row is never marked processed. The event log therefore permanently misreports an applied event as pending, and nothing reconciles it.

findings.notes: The window is real: cancelSubscription (actions.ts:334) commits the cancellation at Lemon Squeezy, and a crash or DB error before the update at actions.ts:342-349 leaves the row showing the old status (the catch at :350 only rethrows). setupWebhook subscribes to subscription_updated (actions.ts:140-144), and processWebhookEvent upserts the row by lemonSqueezyId with status, statusFormatted and endsAt from the provider payload (webhook.ts:111-114, 126-129), so it rewrites every field this action writes. The leftover state is repaired by the provider's webhook. This relies on Lemon Squeezy emitting subscription_updated on cancellation, which the source cannot show.

updateSubscription(id, {pause:{mode:'void'}}) at actions.ts:377 pauses billing at Lemon Squeezy before the DB update at actions.ts:385-393 sets isPaused, and a failure in between leaves isPaused=false. The webhook upsert does not repair this: it hard-codes isPaused: false (webhook.ts:117), so subscription_updated can reconcile status/statusFormatted/endsAt but never isPaused. isPaused drives the UI: actions-dropdown.tsx:52/67 keeps offering 'Pause payments' and never shows 'Unpause payments', and status.tsx:24 relies on it. Nothing else in the app restores the flag. (The webhook overwriting isPaused with false is a separate defect on the normal path too.)

updateSubscription(id, {pause:null}) at actions.ts:421 resumes billing before the DB update at actions.ts:425-433. A failure in between leaves isPaused=true and the old status. The subscription_updated webhook (registered at actions.ts:140-144) upserts status, statusFormatted and endsAt, and writes isPaused: false (webhook.ts:111-117, 126-129). That is exactly the value this action would have written (pause !== null is false), so redelivery covers every field the action writes. This relies on Lemon Squeezy sending subscription_updated on unpause.

updateSubscription(..., {variantId}) at actions.ts:471 switches the plan at Lemon Squeezy before the DB update of planId/price/endsAt at actions.ts:477-484, so a failure in between leaves the old plan in the row. processWebhookEvent resolves planId from the payload's variant_id (webhook.ts:83-86, 121), fetches price via getPrice (webhook.ts:96-104, 116) and writes endsAt (webhook.ts:114), upserting by lemonSqueezyId (webhook.ts:126-129). That covers all three fields the action writes, so the subscription_updated webhook registered at actions.ts:140-144 reconciles the row.

storeWebhookEvent commits a webhookEvent row with processed=false (webhook.ts:31-40) before processWebhookEvent upserts the subscription (webhook.ts:126-129). This is a deliberate store-then-process inbox. If the request crashes or times out in between, route.ts:51 never returns 200, so Lemon Squeezy redelivers. The redelivery stores a fresh event row and re-runs the idempotent onConflictDoUpdate upsert, which repairs the subscription. The only leftover is an orphan unprocessed event row, which nothing in the app reads.

The two commits are the insert of the event row with processed=false (webhook.ts:31-40, schema.ts:71) and the later update to processed=true (webhook.ts:144-150). The intermediate state is exactly what the processed flag is designed to record: a stored event that did not finish processing. A crash between them makes route.ts:49-51 fail without a 200, so Lemon Squeezy redelivers and a new row is processed. The stale row is only an accurate audit record, and no code reads processed.

On the subscription_* path, the subscription upsert (webhook.ts:126-129) commits before the event row is marked processed (webhook.ts:144-150), so a crash in between leaves an applied subscription with an event row still at processed=false. The route then returns no 200 (route.ts:49-51). Lemon Squeezy redelivers, and the redelivery re-applies the idempotent upsert and marks its own new row processed. The leftover stale flag is never read anywhere in src (grep finds no reader of processed/processingError), so it has no functional effect.

reviewQueue.issue: the auditor lists this window as unhandled; the finding labeler classified the matching finding(s) as intended-risk. Both are AI judgments; neither label was changed. A human reviewer should decide and record the outcome in `corrections`.
